_note: Protocol templates the dashboard offers. Each is a pen as dispensed: composition, volume, and the default titration. The clinician can override units and durations per patient without touching this file. Only pens with verified concentrations belong here — a pen whose mg/mL is unknown cannot compute a dose.
injectionSteps: Press the plunger all the way down and hold for 10 seconds

templates.name: Tesamorelin
templates.notes: Rotate within your least reactive zone — see below.
templates.timing: 30-60 minutes before bed, at least 2 hours after eating
templates.monitoring: IGF-1, fasting glucose, lipid panel. IGF-1 at week 8 — target high-normal; reduce the dose if IGF-1 is above 350-400 ng/mL.
templates.escalation: Increase to 2 mg only if tolerated — no joint aches, swelling or carpal-tunnel symptoms.
templates.doseSource: Dr Kendall — 30 mg / 3 mL pen; 1 mg weeks 1-2 then 2 mg, daily

expect.p: These build over time rather than showing up straight away, which catches most people off guard. Tesamorelin does not sting from acidity the way NAD+ does — it activates mast cells in the tissue under your skin, and the histamine they release causes the reaction.
list: Itchy, raised welts that look like mosquito bites
Redness and warmth at the site
expect.note: This is an immune response, not an allergy. It depends on your dose and on where you inject.

expect.h: What the first two months look like
rows: Little or nothing. It is easy to assume you are in the clear.
The first welts appear, and are often mistaken for bad technique.
Reactions become consistent, and some sites are clearly worse than others.
The pattern settles. This is when the steps below start to matter.
expect.note: This is why “rotate your sites” on its own does not fix it. Rotating from day one does not stop the reactions appearing — the tissue is reacting to repeated tesamorelin, not to the needle.

expect.p: Taken 30–60 minutes ahead, an H1 blocker blunts the histamine response.
list: Loratadine (Claritin) 10 mg — if cetirizine makes you sleepy
Diphenhydramine (Benadryl) 25 mg — stronger but sedating, which suits a before-bed injection
expect.note: Most people find this reduces the reaction substantially, and for some it stops the welts entirely.

expect.p: A shallow injection leaves the tesamorelin against the mast-cell-rich layer just under the skin. Going deeper puts distance between them.
list: Use a ½-inch needle and go in at 90°
Pinch firmly to give yourself depth
Aim for the fat pad, not just the space under the skin
expect.note: If the reactions persist even with good depth, message the atelier before changing anything else — there are other options and we would rather adjust it with you.

expect.p: Sites are not equal. From what patients and the wider peptide community report:
rows: Worst — the densest population of mast cells
Varies — fine for some, worse for others

expect.h: When a reaction is more than a reaction
expect.p: A typical tesamorelin reaction stays at the site and settles within an hour or two. Tell us the same day if you see:
list: Welts spreading beyond the injection site
Hives somewhere else on your body
Reactions worsening week after week despite everything above
A site turning hard, hot, or producing pus — that is infection, not histamine
expect.note: Facial swelling, throat tightness or trouble breathing is different — call 911 first, then tell us. If reactions do not settle with an antihistamine and better technique, some people are simply sensitive to tesamorelin, and we will move you to a different GHRH analog.

templates.name: Tirzepatide
templates._source: Atelier Tirzepatide Guide: 17 mg/mL, 1 mL vials. Drawn with an insulin syringe — one unit is 0.01 mL, so a unit delivers 0.17 mg.
templates.storage: Keep the vial in the freezer in a light-filtering zip lock. Do not leave it out more than 24 hours.
templates.notes: Inject on the same day each week. If nausea follows a dose increase, take one Zofran every 6–8 hours as needed. Weigh yourself weekly and tell the atelier if you are losing more than 3–4 lb a week. Increase protein so you lose fat rather than muscle.

injectionStepsSyringe: Take the vial out of the freezer and let it thaw ~5 minutes
Wipe the top of the vial with alcohol
Draw up to {units} units — the dashes on the syringe are units
Wipe the skin on your lower stomach with alcohol
Pinch an inch, insert at 90° and push the plunger
Remove the needle and place it in a sharps container
injectionStepsVial: Take the vial out of the fridge and let it come to room temperature
Wipe the top of the vial with alcohol
Draw up to {units} units — the dashes on the syringe are units
Wipe the skin on your lower stomach with alcohol
Pinch an inch, insert at 90° and push the plunger
Remove the needle and place it in a sharps container

needles: A new disposable pen tip before every single use. Never reuse one — it blunts, which hurts more and damages the tissue.
Take the tip off immediately after you inject. A pen stored with the tip on can leak, and it lets air into the cartridge.
Put the pen cap back on, and put the pen straight back where it lives.
Never share a pen, even with a new tip.
sharps: Used pen tips go in a sharps container, in line with local sharps disposal rules — never the household bin, never a bottle.
Bring the full container to the atelier and we will dispose of it for you.
travel: Carry it on. Never check it — the hold gets cold enough to freeze a pen.
Use an insulated case with a cold pack, and keep a layer between the pack and the pen so it does not freeze against it.
TSA allows medication and cold packs through security. Message us before you fly and we will send a letter on practice letterhead.
wrong: Left out of the fridge — do not guess. Message us with how long and how warm, and we will tell you whether it is still good.
Frozen when it should not have been — do not use it. Freezing breaks the peptide even after it thaws.
Cloudy, discoloured, or with anything floating in it — do not use it. It should be clear.
Dropped — check the cartridge for a crack before you use it. If in doubt, message us.

priming.why: A new pen is primed once, before the very first dose. It clears the air out of the system, gets the medication flowing, and is what makes the dial accurate.
steps: Screw on a new disposable pen tip
Take the protective cover off the pen tip
Hold the pen upright, tip pointing at the ceiling
Press the injection button all the way down
priming.check: Look for a small bead of fluid at the tip. If nothing appears, repeat the same steps until it does. Once you see fluid, the pen is primed.
priming.once: Only before the first dose from a new pen — not before every injection.

handling.storageNote: Tirzepatide is the exception — it lives in the FREEZER, not the fridge, in a light-filtering zip lock. Everything else stays refrigerated and must never freeze.
